title: Multi-Period Portfolio Optimization using Model Predictive Control with Mean-Variance and Risk Parity Frameworks

extraction.methodology_summary: The authors employ a model predictive control (MPC) framework for multi-period portfolio optimization, comparing mean-variance and risk-parity objective functions over a planning horizon. Asset returns and covariance matrices are dynamically forecasted using a hidden Markov model (HMM) fitted via an expectation-maximization algorithm over a rolling 2000-day window. To solve the non-convex risk-parity MPC formulation efficiently and robustly, a successive convex programming algorithm is introduced.
extraction.universe: Ten major asset classes including global/domestic equities, US treasuries and corporate bonds, high yield, commodities, and real estate
key_findings: Multi-period portfolio models using model predictive control (MPC) perform better than their single-period counterparts in the out-of-sample period (2006-2020).
Both mean-variance and risk-parity MPC formulations successfully beat the fixed-mix benchmark.
The multi-period risk parity (MPO RP) strategy achieves an out-of-sample Sharpe ratio of 0.97, while the multi-period mean-variance (MPO) strategy achieves 0.64.
The proposed successive convex program algorithm for risk-parity MPC yields solutions up to 30 times faster and with greater numerical stability than the original non-convex formulation.
limitations: Single-period and multi-period strategies' performance depends heavily on the accuracy of underlying parameter estimation frameworks like the hidden Markov model.
